cells.tense: You're at the wheel right now, and you know which way you're pointing it.
cells.ask: Hand one piece of what you're steering to someone who'd grow it further than you would alone.
cells.core:
You're holding the reins and you're not white-knuckling them. You know what's worth your push and what you can let go of, and both come from the same steadiness. People feel that you've chosen this, not that you're bracing against something. A day like that looks ordinary from the outside — you put your hand to what matters, you take it off when it's done, and the people around you get the calm version of you rather than the braced one.

There's a way you tend what you've built that doesn't drain you and doesn't crowd it — care that lets the thing find its own shape. What this steadiness opens onto is somebody else's growing: give one piece of the work to a person who'd take it somewhere you wouldn't, and let their way of doing it be different from yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering, and you know what to let go of.
cells.verb: knowing what to release and letting it go with a steady hand
cells.place: at the wheel, choosing which way this goes

cells.tense: You're already living past today, bracing for a finish line that hasn't been drawn yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you can honestly call finished today, and let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
You drive hard and you also know when to set it down. You finish a thing, you look at it, you say that's done, and the next hour isn't spent replaying it. The push and the putting-down take turns, and the people working alongside you get to keep up because you're not sprinting ahead of them.

These days the push has the whole seat. You're driving toward a landing you can already picture, and you're gripping every step of the process to force it to arrive on schedule. The calm you'd need to actually finish is being spent on whether you'll get there at all. Method is what steadies this — one honest measure of done, taken today, and nothing done past it.
cells.sheetLine: You're driving to prove you'll arrive, not to arrive.

cells.tense: You're standing back where a decision already got made, still holding the door open.
cells.ask: Put your hand on one thing you've already built and stay with it while it finishes.
cells.core:
You choose and then you move. You say this, not that, and the saying turns into walking — the direction is settled and your feet are already on it. The people with you don't have to guess where you're headed.

The choosing has gone quiet lately and the not-choosing has gotten comfortable. There's a direction that's yours and you're not taking it. You know what you'd pick if you let yourself, and it stays filed under later, so nothing starts. Put your hand on something you already made and hold it steady while it becomes what it is — strength that contains rather than crushes is what pulls your aim back.
cells.sheetLine: You know the way and you're not walking it.

cells.tense: You're deciding direction already, every day, and talking about it as if it decided itself.
cells.ask: Tend one thing you started, at its own pace, and say out loud that you chose it.
cells.core:
This is visible when it's working: you make a call, you say why, and everyone knows the choice was yours to make. You own the direction out loud, which is what lets other people build on it instead of waiting to see what you'll do.

What's happening instead is that you make those calls all day — this project, that offer, this line and not the other — and you file each one under what the situation demanded. The call is real and it's yours; you're just not saying so. Go back a step and care for something you began the way an apprentice would, curious and unhurried, letting it grow at its own speed. Naming one of those choices yours, where someone can hear it, is what hands the wheel back.
